explanation: Sudan held the title until South Sudan split away. Algeria, mostly Sahara, covers about 2.38 million km², just ahead of DR Congo.

claims.text: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
DR Congo, about 2.34 million km², Sudan, about 1.89 million km², and Libya, about 1.76 million km², are each smaller in area than Algeria.
Before South Sudan split from it, Sudan was the largest country in Africa by area.
Most of Algeria lies within the Sahara.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors or warnings for this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; c1 and c4 are superlatives and c2 and c3 carry numbers, all high; c5 is standard ('most of' is a quantity, not a superlative). Datasets: mledoze-countries, region Africa sorted by area: DZA 2,381,741; COD 2,344,858; SDN 1,886,068; LBY 1,759,540 km² (c1 to c3). For c4: SDN 1,886,068 + SSD 619,745 = 2,505,813 km², more than Algeria. Rival test: DR Congo is within 2 per cent of Algeria, so the key rests on measured areas; every figure I know puts Algeria first, as the pinned file does, but the margin is small enough that checker A should add a second source. Sudan is the trap for anyone who learned the map before South Sudan's independence; Libya is big but clearly smaller. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: African geography that school maps everywhere show. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight quotes, explanation of 22 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no match. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: only the narrow DR Congo margin, flagged above. Not marked counterintuitive: the pull towards Sudan or DR Congo is a gap in knowledge more than a confident belief.

claimResults.note: Sorting all region=Africa entries by area puts DZA first, then COD, SDN and LBY.
Pre-2011 Sudan covered today's Sudan plus South Sudan, 2,505,813 km², more than Algeria, today's largest. The 2011 secession itself is from knowledge.

evidence.restatement: The Sahara covers more than four-fifths of Algeria's territory.

issues.note: Not wrong today. But the title passed from Sudan to Algeria only in 2011, so a fact like this can move again; volatility slow with a reviewBy may fit better than evergreen.

editor.reason: Both checks pass with every claim confirmed; high-risk c1 to c4 carry mledoze-countries evidence in both checks (§9.9 rule 3). Lint clean, no myth hits. A's outdated note is answered by the item itself: the ranking moved only with South Sudan's secession, which the explanation defuses, and nothing short of a border change can move it again, so evergreen stands.
